start.card:
A shirt costs $100. On Monday the store raises the price by 25%. On Tuesday the shirt goes on sale: 25% off.
"25%" (say "25 percent") means 25 out of every 100. So 25% of $100 is $25.
Where does the price end up after Tuesday? Pick a guess below.
start.title: Up 25%, Down 25%: the shirt price

afterGuess.card:
You picked "Back to $100". Now find out.
Press "Monday: raise the price 25%" and watch the bar.
afterGuess.title: Up 25%, Down 25%: the shirt price

after.card:
Now: $200.00, down 90% then up 90%, ends at $38.00.
Takeaway: a percent is always a piece of the price it is taken from. Going up and down by the same percent never cancels out: you always end lower.
after.title: Up 25%, Down 25%: the shirt price
